title: Betty Lewis Cromwell (Shinnecock)
summary: Betty Lewis Cromwell was a Shinnecock community member documented in a photograph caption from a December 6, 1997 Shinnecock Nation Cultural Center and Museum fundraiser.
content:
Betty Lewis Cromwell is documented as a Shinnecock cultural advocate and founding board member of the Shinnecock Nation Cultural Center and Museum project, as well as in a photograph from its December 6, 1997 fundraiser. The currently cited sources do not establish her birth or death dates.

The current verified source support is brief. The history therefore preserves her name and Shinnecock community connection without adding unsupported dates, school memories, family details, or stories not yet supported by reliable sources.1

Historical Context

The 1997 fundraiser context connects Cromwell with Shinnecock cultural-center public history and community efforts to sustain cultural institutions.1

References

  1. John A. Strong, We Are Still Here! The Algonquian Peoples of Long Island Today, p. 97.
  2. Beverly Jensen, Shinnecock Indian Nation, pending source review for any additional biographical detail.
why_this_matters: Betty Lewis Cromwell shows why community photographs, fundraiser records, and museum history matter. Even a brief source mention can help keep Shinnecock women visible in public memory when handled carefully and without inventing unsupported biography.
